title: ASAS-3 and TESS eclipse times (2000-2026) show common period changes in 77 of 304 detached binaries; if these are light-travel effects, a third or more have third stars with decade orbits
abstract: A campaign screen (SCI 521b99d2) found third-body eclipse timing variations in 14 of 557 detached southern binaries (P = 5-22 d) from TESS data of 2018-2026 only. We used archival ASAS-3 V photometry of 2000-2009 as independent timing data and extended the baseline to 26 years. For 398 binaries we fitted ASAS-3 eclipse templates and measured primary and secondary times in chunks of at most 120 d. A link test compares the ASAS-3 epoch offset and period with the TESS ephemeris; TESS timing variations and ASAS-3 scatter enter as noise. Of 304 binaries with at least five ASAS-3 times, 88 fail at p < 0.001 (0.3 expected by chance). In 77 (25 percent) the primary and secondary eclipses move together, as light travel time (LTTE) from a third star causes; 11 show apsidal motion. 65 of the 77 were quiet in TESS. With errors inflated by the split-half scatter, 60 remain. The TESS third bodies pass the test in 6 of 12 testable binaries, and joint TESS and ASAS-3 LTTE fits give outer periods of 4.0-16.9 yr and more than 27 yr; ASAS 063202-6750.7 follows one 16.9-yr orbit. Simulated LTTE signals injected into the real sampling reproduce the observed epoch offsets (KS p = 0.39) and Doppler velocity changes dv = c dP/P (KS p = 0.33; median 3.4 km/s). The test detects third stars with outer periods of about 10-60 yr with probability up to 0.73. If all common-mode changes are LTTE, at least 35 percent (27 percent with inflated errors) of these binaries have such a third star. A field-like companion period distribution would need a third star for almost every binary. Checks: split-half calibration (robust sd 1.03), a 1.7-min ASAS-3 clock offset, ACVS period signs (p = 0.02). Gaia DR3 RUWE does not differ significantly. Limits: no spectroscopy; the cause of each change is not proven; population numbers depend on assumed mass ratios, eccentricities and pair masses; LTTE eccentricities are not constrained.
